% ─── FRAME 2: Motivation & scope ─────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Motivation \& scope}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.55\textwidth}
    \begin{itemize}
      \item \textbf{Deliberate simplification:} readout \emph{only} at the
            two ends ($\pm X$ faces); all other faces wrapped in Mylar.
      \item \textbf{Goals:}
        \begin{itemize}
          \item Isolate end-readout contribution.
          \item Characterize multi-component attenuation with Mylar.
          \item Benchmark the SUM4 timing estimator on a clean geometry.
        \end{itemize}
      \item \NPos\ beam positions ($x=-690\ldots+690$\,mm),
            \NEv\ $\mu^-$ events per position.
    \end{itemize}
    \column{0.43\textwidth}
    \begin{block}{This study}
      \textbf{End-only + Mylar} = extreme limit.
      Photons either exit to an end SiPM or are absorbed by Mylar
      after multiple reflections.
    \end{block}
    \begin{alertblock}{\small No TB counterpart}
      \small This configuration has \alert{no direct test-beam counterpart}
      (April-2026 TB used top readout + Tyvek).
    \end{alertblock}
    \begin{alertblock}{\small Electronic jitter not included}
      \small SPTR $\oplus$ FastIC jitter are post-processing steps,
      not folded into $\sigma_t$ shown here.
    \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ─── FRAME 3: Geometry & simulation setup ─────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Geometry \& simulation setup}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.55\textwidth}
    \begin{itemize}
      \item \textbf{Bar:} EJ-204 (OPSC-101),
            $\BarLen \times 60 \times 10$\,mm$^3$.
      \item \textbf{Longitudinal axis:} $X$ ($-700$ to $+700$\,mm).
      \item \textbf{End-left SiPMs} (IDs 0--7): $-X$ face.
            \textbf{End-right SiPMs} (IDs 8--15): $+X$ face.
      \item \textbf{Wrapping:} Mylar on $\pm Y$ and $\pm Z$ faces;
            $R=\MylarR$, specular lobe $=\MylarSL$,
            $\sigma_\alpha=\MylarSA^\circ$.
      \item \textbf{Readout:} SUM4 leading-edge at 4\,PE;
            groups $\{0\text{--}3\}/\{4\text{--}7\}$ (left),
            $\{8\text{--}11\}/\{12\text{--}15\}$ (right).
      \item \textbf{Estimator:}
            $\sigma_\mathrm{single} = \sigma_{LR}/\sqrt{2}$.
      \item \textbf{Beam:} $\mu^-$, 1\,GeV, normal incidence.
    \end{itemize}
    \column{0.43\textwidth}
    \begin{block}{Key parameters}
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{ll}
        \toprule
        Scint.~yield  & \ScintYield \\
        Emission peak & \PeakEm\,nm \\
        Bulk $\lambda$ & \LamBulk\,cm \\
        $n$           & \RefrIdx \\
        $\tau_r / \tau_d$ & \TauRise/\TauDecay \\
        Mylar $R$     & \MylarR \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}
    \end{block}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

  \begin{columns}[T]

    \begin{alertblock}{\small Observation}
      \small Log-scale reveals two regimes:
      prompt near-end region (steep)

      Mylar recirculates but also absorbs.
    \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}

% ─── FRAME 5: Bulk vs effective attenuation ──────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Two attenuation lengths: datasheet vs.\ system measurement}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.50\textwidth}
    \begin{block}{$\lambda_\mathrm{bulk}$ = \LamBulk\,cm (datasheet)}
      \small
      \textbf{Material property.} Loaded as \texttt{ABSLENGTH} in
      \texttt{Materials.cc:99}.
      Probability of straight-line absorption in the plastic.
      \textbf{Knows nothing} about bar geometry or reflectors.
    \end{block}
    \begin{exampleblock}{$\lambda_\mathrm{eff}$ (what we fit)}
      \small
      \textbf{System observable}: slope of NPE vs.\ distance at end.
      Combines bulk absorption \emph{and} geometry \emph{and} reflection losses.
      Always $\lambda_\mathrm{eff} < \lambda_\mathrm{bulk}$.
      \textbf{These two quantities are not directly comparable.}
    \end{exampleblock}
    \column{0.48\textwidth}
    \begin{alertblock}{Why a single exponential fails}
      \small
      Three numbers that should agree if $N_0 e^{-d/\lambda}$ held:
      \begin{enumerate}
        \item Two-point ($d$=10\,mm $\to$ 700\,mm): $\lambda\approx19$\,cm
        \item Single-exp fit: $\lambda\approx\LamSingleL$, $N_0=\NzeroSingleL$\,PE
        \item Actual NPE at $d\approx0$: \ActualNearL\,PE
      \end{enumerate}
      Items (2) and (3) disagree by $\approx3.6\times$.
      $\chi^2/\mathrm{ndf} = \ChiSingleL$ confirms the model is wrong.
      \medskip

      \textbf{Physical reason:} the NPE profile has two components ---
      prompt (short-range) and recirculated floor (Mylar-sustained).
    \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ─── FRAME 6: Attenuation curve (exp+offset fit) ─────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Attenuation: two-component fit and tail $\lambda$}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.65\textwidth}
    \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig_attenuation.png}
    \column{0.33\textwidth}
    \begin{block}{Exp+offset model (left side)}
      \small
      $N(d) = A\,e^{-d/\lambda_p} + C$
      \medskip

      $\lambda_p = \LamPromptL$ (prompt)\\
      $C = \CFloorL$ (recirculated floor)\\
      $\chi^2/\mathrm{ndf} = \ChiExpoffL$
      \medskip

      Tail fit ($d>\DTail$\,cm):\\
      $\lambda_\mathrm{tail} = \LamTailL$
    \end{block}
    \begin{alertblock}{\small $\lambda_\mathrm{eff} \neq \lambda_\mathrm{bulk}$}
      \small \LamBulk\,cm (bulk) is the material ABSLENGTH.
      $\lambda_p\approx21$\,cm and $\lambda_\mathrm{tail}\approx42$\,cm
      are \emph{system} observables: dominated by
      geometry + Mylar losses, not bulk absorption.
    \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ─── FRAME 7: Two-component fit diagnostics ──────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Single-exp vs.\ exp+offset: model comparison}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.65\textwidth}
    \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig_attenuation_twocomp.png}
    \column{0.33\textwidth}
    \begin{block}{Key diagnostics}
      \tiny
      \begin{tabular}{lrr}
        \toprule
        Model & $\lambda$ (cm) & $\chi^2/\mathrm{ndf}$ \\
        \midrule
        Single-exp  & \LamSingleL  & \ChiSingleL \\
        Exp+offset  & \LamPromptL  & \ChiExpoffL \\
        $\lambda_\mathrm{tail}$ ($d>\DTail$\,cm) & \LamTailL & \ChiTailL \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}
    \end{block}
    \begin{alertblock}{\small Inconsistency proof}
      \small
      Red star: actual NPE at $d\approx0$ is \ActualNearL\,PE.\\
      Single-exp $N_0 = \NzeroSingleL$\,PE (red dashed).\\
      Factor $\approx3.6$ inconsistency.\\
      Single-exp $\chi^2/\mathrm{ndf}=\ChiSingleL$ confirms failure.
    \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ─── FRAME 8: Far-end light yield ────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Far-end light yield: where reflector quality matters}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.55\textwidth}
    \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig_far_end_yield.png}
    \column{0.43\textwidth}
    \begin{block}{Center-of-bar NPE ($|x|\leq100$\,mm)}
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{lrr}
        \toprule
        Config & $R$ & NPE \\
        \midrule
        End-only+Mylar & \MylarR & \NPETailMylar\,PE \\
        EndTop & \EndtopR & \NPETailET\,PE \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}
      \medskip

      Ratio EndTop/Mylar $\approx 2.5\times$.
    \end{block}
    \begin{alertblock}{\small Physical interpretation}
      \small
      Both configs see photons after $\geq60$\,cm propagation
      and many reflections.
      At $R=\MylarR$ (Mylar), each bounce absorbs 10\%: cumulative loss
      dominates. At $R=\EndtopR$, only 2\% per bounce.
      \medskip
      \textbf{Reflector quality, not $\lambda_\mathrm{bulk}$,
      controls the recirculated light level.}
    \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ─── FRAME 9: Apples-to-apples comparison ────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Apples-to-apples: End-only+Mylar vs.\ EndTop}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.65\textwidth}
    \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig_endtop_comparison.png}
    \column{0.33\textwidth}
    \begin{block}{Identical pipeline}
      \small
      Both datasets processed with the \textbf{same} end-SiPM-only
      selection, attenuation models, and tail-fit range.
    \end{block}
    \begin{block}{$\lambda_\mathrm{tail}$ comparison ($d>\DTail$\,cm)}
      \tiny
      \begin{tabular}{lr}
        \toprule
        Config & $\lambda_\mathrm{tail}$ \\
        \midrule
        End-only+Mylar & \LamTailL \\
        EndTop & \LamTailET \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}
      \medskip
      
      \textbf{Similar slope} --- dominated by geometry, not reflector type.
    \end{block}
    \begin{alertblock}{\small Conclusion}
      \small
      $\lambda_\mathrm{tail}$ does \emph{not} distinguish configs;
      the NPE \emph{amplitude} does.
      End-only+Mylar has $\approx2.5\times$ less light at center
      due to $R=\MylarR$ vs $R=\EndtopR$.
    \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ─── FRAME 11: FPT vs t50 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{FPT vs.\ $t_{50}$: comparing timing estimators}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.65\textwidth}
    \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig_fpt_vs_t50.png}
    \column{0.33\textwidth}
    \begin{block}{FPT vs.\ $t_{50}$}
      \small
      FPT: minimum of photon arrival times per event.\\
      $t_{50}$: median --- less sensitive to the
      $N$-dependent statistical minimum.
      \medskip
      $t_{50}$ systematically later than FPT;
      offset grows with distance.
    \end{block}
    \begin{alertblock}{\small $v_\mathrm{eff}$ bias}
      \small
      FPT $v_\mathrm{eff} = \VeffFPT$ (apparent, biased
      by $N$-dependent statistical minimum).\\
      SUM4 $\Delta t$ gives $v_\mathrm{eff} = \VeffSUMfour$ (robust).
    \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

    \begin{alertblock}{\small FPT anomaly}

      $v_\mathrm{eff}^\mathrm{FPT} > c/n$

      Artifact: FPT = statistical minimum of $N$ photon

    \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ─── FRAME 14: Photon budget ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Photon budget --- End-only + Mylar}
  \begin{columns}[T]

        Detected (PDE) & \BudgetDet \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}
    \end{block}
    \begin{alertblock}{\small Mylar loss dominates}
      \small
      Each Mylar bounce: $(1-R)=\MylarR$ absorbed.
      $\Rightarrow$ Over many bounces in a thin bar,
      cumulative loss $\gg$ bulk loss.
      This explains $\lambda_p \approx 21$\,cm $\ll$ \LamBulk\,cm.
    \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ─── FRAME 15: Summary ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Summary}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.55\textwidth}
    \begin{block}{Key results}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item \textbf{Two attenuation lengths:}
              $\lambda_\mathrm{bulk}=\LamBulk$\,cm (ABSLENGTH, material property);
              $\lambda_p\approx21$\,cm (prompt system component);
              $\lambda_\mathrm{tail}\approx\LamTailL$ (tail, comparable metric).
              These are \emph{not} the same quantity.
        \item \textbf{Single-exp fails:}
              $\chi^2/\mathrm{ndf}=\ChiSingleL$;
              $N_0$ inconsistency factor $\approx3.6\times$.
              Two-component model required.
        \item \textbf{Reflector $R$ controls tail NPE:}
              End-only+Mylar ($R=\MylarR$): \NPETailMylar\,PE at center;
              EndTop ($R=\EndtopR$): \NPETailET\,PE.
              Ratio $\approx2.5\times$.
        \item $\lambda_\mathrm{tail}$ is \emph{equal} in both configs ---
              the NPE amplitude is the distinguishing observable.
        \item $\sigma_t^\mathrm{intr.}$: \SigmaAtZero\ (center)
              to \SigmaAtMsixnine\ (ends) --- intrinsic only.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{block}
    \column{0.43\textwidth}
    \begin{block}{Next steps}
      \begin{enumerate}
        \item Fold in electronic jitter:
              $\sigma_\mathrm{SPTR}=106$\,ps
              $\oplus\,\sigma_\mathrm{FastIC}=10$\,ps.
        \item Leading-edge time-walk correction.
        \item Scan Mylar $R\in[0.85,0.95]$ to map
              NPE yield vs.\ reflector quality.
        \item Scan with Tyvek for direct comparison
              to April-2026 TB configuration.
      \end{enumerate}
    \end{block}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

  \small
  All fits weighted by per-point SEM.
  Errors from covariance matrix, scaled by $\sqrt{\chi^2/\mathrm{ndf}}$ when $>1$.
  Tail fit: $d>\DTail$\,cm only.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Appendix D: method \& caveats}
  \small
  \begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Geometry:} Bar $1400\times60\times10$\,mm$^3$; long axis $X$.
          End SiPMs on $\pm X$; Mylar on $\pm Y,\pm Z$.
    \item \textbf{SUM4 trigger:} leading-edge at 4\,PE.
          Groups $\{0\text{--}3\}/\{4\text{--}7\}$ (left);
          $\{8\text{--}11\}/\{12\text{--}15\}$ (right).
    \item \textbf{$\sigma_t$ is intrinsic only:} optical + estimator;
          SPTR ($\approx106$\,ps) and FastIC ($\approx10$\,ps)
          not folded in.
    \item \textbf{SiPM naming:} \texttt{\SiPMModelPDE}
          is used \emph{only} for the PDE curve;
          physical device is the single-element \textbf{\SiPMModel}.
    \item \textbf{No TB counterpart:} April-2026 TB used top readout
          + Tyvek wrapping $\neq$ end-only + Mylar.
    \item \textbf{Longitudinal axis $= X$} (not $Z$ or $Y$).
    \item \textbf{Yield:} OPSC-101 loaded with \ScintYield\ in
          \texttt{Materials.cc:100} --- matches Eljen EJ-204 datasheet Aug~2023.
    \item \textbf{EndTop reference:} EXEC\_07, \NEv\ events/position,
          same 31 positions. Side reflectors $R=\EndtopR$ (BarSkinReflector),
          NOT Mylar.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}
